Alina —

Thanks for the clear list. We put together a concise implementation plan and an activation cadence that maps to your asks. See the attached "redwood-implementation-plan-v1.pdf" and "integration-checklist.xlsx" — highlights below:

Master timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (prep): NDA/contract signature, network peering requests, KMS onboarding.
- Week 1 (integration sprint 1): API connectivity, test environment provisioning, initial model selection and config.
- Week 2 (integration sprint 2): Prefix/caching validation, telemetry hooks, access control verification.
- Week 3 (pilot): 1% traffic canary for 72 hours, automated rollback tests, load conformance.
- Week 4 (scale): Ramp to 10% for 48 hours, verify billing/instrumentation; scheduled cutoff/maintenance window agreed.
- Week 5 (cutover): 50%/day increments to 100% with pre-specified SLO checks; post-cutover validation and 7-day observation period.

Canary & rollback policy (summary):
- Start at 1% of production traffic for 72 hours with health checks every 15 minutes.
- Failure triggers: error rate >2% sustained over 5 minutes OR median latency regression >30% vs baseline OR critical quality regression on seed prompts.
- Auto-fallback: requests routed to stable model variant + alerting to on-call. Manual rollback path in 15 minutes.

Integration touchpoints:
- Network: peering + static IP allowlist (action: Novastream network team to open firewall rules, estimated lead time 3–5 business days).
- Auth: KMS key material exchange and role binding (we've detailed steps in attachment).
- Telemetry: ingestion token and destination for traces/metrics (we support Datadog/Prometheus).
- Data flow: staging dataset push for prompt/response QA (we recommend a sanitized 10k sample).

Prerequisites from Novastream:
- Completed peering request form + CIDR ranges.
- Service account for KMS integration and 2 admin contacts.
- Test dataset and prioritized prompt set for quality gating.

Action items & next steps:
1) Please confirm the peering request owner and desired maintenance windows.
2) If the timeline above looks reasonable, we'd schedule a 60-minute kickoff with SRE and integration leads on Thursday.
3) We will provide an editable sprint-gates CSV (attached as sprint-gates.csv) for you to annotate.

I'll let Laura loop in specifics on telemetry thresholds and Marissa on account provisioning.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Email: david.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0149

Quick follow-ups from infra/telemetry perspective — replying inline here.

> Week 3 (pilot): 1% traffic canary for 72 hours, automated rollback tests, load conformance.

We should be explicit on: why 72 hours and what telemetry thresholds we will use for progression. I propose:
- Canary duration: minimum 72 hours AND at least one full business cycle (Mon-Fri) to capture weekday load patterns.
- Progression checks: 0 min: successful connection and auth checks; 4 hours: no spike in 5xx errors; 24 hours: latency P50/P99 within expected bounds; 72 hours: no quality regressions on the seed prompts.

> Failure triggers: error rate >2% sustained over 5 minutes OR median latency regression >30% vs baseline

Recommend adding a combined rule: sustained error rate >1.5% AND a concurrent 20% latency regression over 10 minutes should trigger a pause and human review (reduces noisy rollbacks).

Telemetry hooks we will need from Novastream:
- Destination for traces (Datadog API key)
- A short list of 25 seed prompts for quality checks
- Baseline latency numbers for current production path for comparison

I'll append these into the Drive doc and add expected metric names. David/Marissa — can we confirm the default canary policy in the UI will be set to manual promotion unless otherwise requested?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
